source_text: Baptisma perfecte homines innovare, si quidem Apostolus testis sit, qui per lavacrum aquae Ecclesiam de Gentibus sanctam fieri immaculatamque testatur. Sanctum quoque Spiritum mentes bonas in antiquis adiuvasse, dicente Propheta ad Deum: Spiritus tuus bonus deducet me in viam rectam. Omnes quoque Prophetas et Apostolos vel sanctos et evangelicos et antiquos, quibus Deus testimonium perhibet, non in comparatione sceleratorum, sed regula virtutum iustos fuisse. In futuro autem tempore mercedem esse factorum bonorum atque malorum, nec tamen ibi posse quemquam quae hic contempserit implere mandata, quia dixerit Apostolus: Omnes nos manifestari oportet ante tribunal Christi, ut reportet unusquisque propria corporis, prout gessit, sive bonum sive malum
pass_a_gloss: that baptism perfectly makes human beings new, the Apostle being a witness, who testifies that through the washing of water the Church from the nations is made holy and unstained. That the Holy Spirit also helped good minds in ancient times, the Prophet saying to God: Your good Spirit will lead me on a straight road. That all Prophets and Apostles, or saints both of the Gospel and of old, to whom God bears testimony, were just not by comparison with criminals but by the rule of virtues. That in the time to come there is a wage of good deeds and of bad, yet no one can there fulfill the commandments he despised here, because the Apostle said: We must all be made manifest before the tribunal of Christ, so that each may bring back the things of the body, according as he has done, whether good or evil.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Baptism makes people completely new. The apostle is a witness to this, for he testifies that through the washing of water the church gathered from the nations is made holy and spotless (Ephesians 5:26–27).
The Holy Spirit also helped good minds in ancient times, as the prophet says to God: “Your good Spirit will lead me on a straight path” (Psalm 143:10; LXX Psalm 142:10).
All the prophets, apostles, and saints, both of the New Testament and of the Old, to whom God bears witness, were righteous by the standard of virtue, not by comparison with criminals.

In the time to come there is recompense for good deeds and for bad ones. But no one can fulfill there the commandments that they disregarded here, because the apostle said: “We must appear before Christ’s judgment seat, so that each person may receive what belongs to the body, according to what they have done, whether good or evil” (2 Corinthians 5:10).

choices.why: Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.
Keep the rite-name; Julian says praise of baptism is being used to smuggle natural evil.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.
